Based on the circuit diagram provided:
- The input is a sinusoidal AC voltage $V_i$ varying between $+5\text{ V}$ and $-5\text{ V}$.
- A Zener diode with $V_z = 2\text{ V}$ connected in parallel with the output (along with a silicon diode in series or similar clamping configuration as shown).
- **Output Waveform ($V_o$):** The circuit acts as a clipper/voltage limiter. The positive half-cycle is clipped at the combined barrier/Zener voltage limit, and the negative half-cycle is limited by the $2\text{ V}$ Zener breakdown/forward drop. Thus, the output waveform is clipped symmetrically at $\pm 2\text{ V}$ (or corresponding limits based on diode orientation), flattening the peaks of the sinusoidal wave.
